struck: Only 3 of the 299 months since late 2001 were lower, all in 2021.
use: Only 2 other months since late 2001 were lower: May and June 2021.

struck: At the 2006 high it was about 83 percent.
use: In mid-2006 it was about 83 percent, the highest in 25 years.

struck: Horry County has about 41,000 condo units in about 1,480 condo regimes. Half the units are in the 104 complexes of 100 units or more.
use: Horry County has about 41,000 condo units. Almost half of them, about 20,000, are in large complexes of 100 units or more.

struck: Half of the county's condo complexes have 8 units or fewer.
use: (cut it: the complex count rests on legal-description names, split by phase and by typing errors)

pattern: \bsomeone's main home\b|\bthe rest are rentals, second homes(?: and| or)? vacation homes\b
struck: Our count: about 1 in 5 condos is someone's main home. The rest are rentals, second homes and vacation homes, taxed at 6 percent.
use: About 1 in 5 condo units is taxed at the 4 percent rate for its owner's legal residence. The rest are taxed at 6 percent, the rate for rentals, second homes and any home whose owner has not claimed the legal-residence rate.

pattern: \b(?:three|3) times as long to sell\b|\bcondos take[^.]{0,40}\blong(?:er)? to sell\b
struck: Condos take about three times as long to sell as houses.
use: About 2,660 condos are for sale in Horry County, about 12 months of sales at last year's pace. For houses and townhouses it is about 4 months.

struck: Most condos for sale allow nightly rentals.
use: About 7 in 10 condos for sale say they allow short-term rentals.

pattern: \b(?:condos|units)(?: for sale)? (?:take|qualify for|can get|are eligible for) (?:an )?FHA\b
struck: Few condos for sale take an FHA or VA loan.
use: About 1 in 9 condo listings (307) say they accept FHA, but HUD's list holds only 9 approved condo projects in Horry County. We confirm the building with the lender before you offer.

struck: A home that is not the owner's legal residence, which includes every rental, is taxed on 6 percent of its value.
use: A home that is not its owner's legal residence, such as a unit rented out year-round or a second home, is taxed on 6 percent of its value.

struck: The owner's legal residence is taxed on 4 percent, and loses it if rented more than 72 days in a year.
use: A legal residence rented out more than 72 days in a calendar year loses the 4 percent rate, unless its owner is on active military duty under orders.

struck: The unit's own insurance is about $970 a year at the top of one agency's South Carolina range for a condo unit policy ($36 to $81 a month).
use: (cut it: an insurance agency's figure, struck on /invest/run-the-numbers/; say we get a quote on the exact unit before you offer)

struck: Total about $19,000 a year before the loan, utilities the fee does not cover, management and cleaning.
use: Total about $18,100 a year before insurance, the loan, utilities the fee does not cover, management and cleaning.

struck: Outside city limits the tax would be about $4,100.
use: Outside city limits, at the base unincorporated rate, it would be about $4,100; some fire districts add more.

struck: Property tax at the rental rate inside the City of Myrtle Beach about $5,200.
use: Property tax at the rental rate inside the City of Myrtle Beach, before the 25 percent exemption a rental buyer may claim: about $5,200.

struck: Fannie Mae, which buys most conventional loans, will not buy a loan on a unit in a building run like a hotel.
use: Fannie Mae, one of the two companies that buy conventional loans, will not buy a loan on a unit in a building run like a hotel, even if each unit is owned separately.

struck: Signs it lists: a front desk or registration, daily or short-term rentals, daily cleaning, central key systems.
use: Signs it lists: registration services, the HOA or its manager renting units by the day or for short stays, daily cleaning, central key systems, a rental pool, or rent shared with the HOA or a rental company.

struck: or in a building that needs critical repairs (for example, unfunded repairs over $10,000 a unit due within 12 months).
use: or in a building that needs critical repairs, for example repairs over $10,000 a unit due within 12 months that no special assessment pays for.

pattern: \bbehind only tax liens and (?:recorded )?mortgages\b(?! and other)|\bahead of every(?:thing| other lien)? except (?:property )?tax(?:es| liens)? and (?:recorded )?mortgages\b(?! and other)
struck: Under South Carolina's condo law, unpaid assessments are a lien on the unit, behind only tax liens and recorded mortgages.
use: Under South Carolina's condo law, unpaid assessments are a lien on the unit that ranks ahead of every other lien except property tax liens and recorded mortgages and other recorded liens.

struck: Other homes: 10.9 percent in a high-risk flood zone.
use: About 1 in 10 other homes sold (10.4 percent) sat in a high-risk flood zone.

use: Story: a house sale and his savings bought three oceanfront condos.

struck: A rental in the busiest quarter keeps about $28,000.
use: A rental at the top-quarter mark for income, rented all year, keeps about $28,000.

struck: Two-bedroom rental: About $20,000 a year
use: Typical two-bedroom nightly rental, before costs: About $20,000 a year
